_about: C2: the authored story content of the one Tiro day the slice ships (docs/campaign/05-c2-slice-story-bible-and-script.md). Inert until T27 reads the lines and T28 reads the scenes. A missing, unreadable or non-version-1 file is skipped with a warning and the day plays one line per beat from strings.json (each beat's 'fallback'), which is how it plays today. Session pacing and story text only: no combat number, no pinned value. Every line is 10 words or fewer (Tests/DayTests.cpp) and every stone label 5 words or fewer.
_status: draft for the owner's ruling (C2 decisions D1-D4). No audio asset exists for any cue; voice is additive and the day is complete as text.
_cueSheet: docs/campaign/05-c2-slice-story-bible-and-script.md section 9. Every line carries a cue id; the id is also what the strings.json _story.* marker becomes (section 10).
_budget: floorS <= naturalS <= maxS. Story total: 54 s floor, 213 s natural, 242 s max. With the 63 s teach and the pinned 145-235 s fight band that is 4.4 min rushed, 7.0-8.5 min natural, 9.0 min max (section 4).
_when: null means always. Otherwise { flag, op (eq|gte|lte), value }: the clause shape of docs/campaign/04-vr-campaign-design.md section 4. Variants are evaluated in file order and the FIRST MATCH WINS, so a default variant is last and carries when: null. A clause naming a flag that does not exist does not match and is never an error. Every flag used here is one the session already writes (Session/DayFlow.cpp:347-358, :385).

beats._about: A static tableau of the ford. Unvoiced in the recommended cue count: block P is cut first. Nobody explains the collaring; the player reads it. Needs day.json prologueMaxS 10 -> 45 (T28).

lines.text: The ford. Four mages held the line.
The legion they held it for closed four collars.
Rome calls this the Games. The collar calls it rent.

scenes._about: WRAPS THE PICK THAT ALREADY EXISTS AND MUST NOT BREAK IT. The build already offers Leviathan or Rain of Orbs here through PlayerPreset.Pick with labels pick.tideOrb.A/.B and pick.continue (SessionFlow.cpp:1536-1612). C2 adds Ophel's framing and nothing else: the stones, the 0.40 s hold, the timeout and the tideOrb branch effect stay exactly as they are. The labels are the EXISTING strings, which already read in Cassia's register - 'if it comes' and 'rather' are the conditional hedges characters.json gives her, at no extra words.

scenes._about: Ophel tells the player how to fight the semifinal, and the when picks WHICH lesson from how bout 2 actually went - the VR identity the campaign design asks for. OPH-05 pre-warns the Sunfall one bout early, so Brennic's second taunt is a reminder and not a surprise. The choice is a STANCE, NOT A STAT: neither option changes a combat number, which would mean touching signed data. The stones are recorded so the tablet and a future eve scene can refer to how the player chose to meet him.

Variant 3B exists because the slice must have something to say to a player who LOST AND CAME BACK, and 'He will remember that' is information, not comfort - Ophel's register is footnotes, and the crowd carries approval so the cast never has to. 3A and 3B are distinguished by attempts, which the session already writes.

taunts._about: Two HP-gated phases at 66 % and 33 %; the second opens with fire_sunfall, UNBLOCKABLE (combat.vr.json rivals.brennic.phases). So BRE-02 is not flavour, it is the warning for an attack the player must not try to absorb. NO TEXT is shown for a taunt: the player is mid-duel with both hands committed and a line on the rail during a Sunfall telegraph competes with the exact thing it warns about. If voice is declined (D4) these are CUT, not converted to text.

Brennic orders; Lio mocks. Neither names a colour, because the black core and red rim are already on screen - the line tells the player what to DO, which is what a cold player misses.

chorus._about: A swell. The overlay data already says a break 'swells the crowd' (combat.vr.json rivals._about).
A short bark of approval, under 1 s, no pitch climb.
A low murmur falling away. Mercy, not booing.
The only full roar in the day, by design: it is the payoff the aftermath line refuses to give in words, and the beat the submission video should end on.

septima.register: ritual, third person; never says 'I'; addresses the player as 'Tide'

venno.register: genial showman; plays to the crowd, not the player; never cruel, always selling

ophel.register: dry, scholarly, footnotes; understated; gives information, never encouragement

brennic.register: hard-headed, aggressive, stronger under tension; short sentences

lio.register: restless, free, contemptuous of rules; mocking, light

cassia._about: The player. DELIBERATELY SILENT: no voiced line in the slice. Not a budget cut - the player's hands are the player's, and a voice put in her mouth competes with them. Her register governs every stone label, which are her thoughts.

_comfort: Every speaker is inside the front +/-70 deg, or +/-40 deg in narrow view, and no line is head-locked (docs/campaign/04-vr-campaign-design.md section 2; plan section 6.1). Text is world-locked on the dais rail, one line at a time.
_neverSay: 'you died', 'death', or blood as the price of losing - below the Summa every loss is missio, the crowd's mercy
loop language: 'again', 'this time', 'reset', 'the last day of every loop' - TV removed loops (plan D2)
a proper noun with no tent or role attached: 'Brennic of the Ember', never bare 'Brennic'
K-ford-betrayal as an on-screen revelation - the prologue SHOWS the collaring; nobody explains it
K-wardstones-drink or the Breaking - a Summa ending the slice does not reach (C2 decision D5)
'sine missione' - reserved for high tiers, not built
a line that tells the player they did well - the crowd carries approval, the cast carries information
